newsitem.title: VATICAN: Russian Catholics finally get their catechism.
newsitem.headline: Russian Catholics finally get their catechism.

text.p: Russian Catholics, long persecuted under the Soviet Union, were given the first catechism in their own language on Tuesday.

Archbishop Tadeusz Kondrusiewicz, the Vatican's Apostolic Administrator in Moscow, told a news conference he hoped the book -- which codifies the Catholic faith -- would help "the renewal of spiritual life" in Russia.
The translation took nearly four years to complete following the publication in 1992 of the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the first major compendium of the Catholic faith in more than 400 years.
Since 1992 the Catechism has been published in most major western languages and has become an international bestseller, with more than seven million copies printed.
Kondrusiewicz said there were now 91 parishes in European Russia to serve 300,000 Catholics but about half still had no churches or chapels to worship in.
The Catechism confirms essential beliefs but brings the Catholic Church up to date with modern sins and temptations, such as tax evasion and issues of bio-ethics.

Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger said he hoped the Russian-language catechism would help improve the sometimes difficult relations with the Russian Orthodox Church because Orthodox Christians would be able to learn more about the Catholic faith.

The Catholic and Orthodox Churches in the former Soviet Union are at odds over the restitution of Catholic property confiscated under communism and Orthodox allegations that the Catholics are using new-found freedoms to poach believers.
Kondrusiewicz said Russian believers were praying that Pope John Paul could eventually visit Moscow and other parts of Russia.
Diplomats say such a trip will be difficult to arrange until Catholic-Orthodox relations improve.
